Subject: Quick follow-up & next steps from today — RTBF details

Hi Katie / Carlos,

Thanks again for taking time today — helpful call. Quick recap and three next steps so we stay aligned on Nova's RTBF requirements: 

Recap (what I heard):
- You need a documented deletion journey for user-initiated RTBF that covers immediate application data deletion, purge from hot KV caches, and backup removal timelines.
- Legal requires clear evidence (audit logs + confirmation) for each deletion request, and an option for shorter data residency windows for certain pilot cohorts.
- Backups are a blocker: Nova cannot accept a ~90-day immutable backup retention for pilot data — you need clarity on how backups are handled and any possible carve-outs.

Action items / next steps:
1) I'll send our RTBF playbook + short summary of how backups are handled today (see attached RTBF_Process_Summary_v2.pdf).
2) Please fill the attached evidence template (nova_evidence_request.xlsx) with two sample user IDs so we can map the end-to-end signals we would provide.
3) I'll loop in legal and our privacy ops (cc'd) to propose an exception path and SLA for pilot cohorts.

Wanted to call out one thing up front: our typical backup retention policy is 30 days for short-term snapshots, with immutable archival up to customer-configured retention. We can discuss a limited exception for pilot-scoped data if Nova can agree to a narrower scope and signed attestation.

I'll wait for one or two sample IDs and we can schedule a short tech deep-dive later this week.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the summary — appreciate the clarity. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Backup window: Our security team will not sign off on any solution that keeps patient-identifiable backups longer than 30 days unless we have documented deletion guarantees and an auditable purge procedure that triggers for pilot cohorts.
- Evidence: We need the deletion confirmation to include: timestamped audit entry, actor id (service account), scope (model, prompt, user_id), and confirmation when data is removed from any cold archives.
- Residency: Pilot data must remain in us-west region; any cross-region replication needs an opt-in checkbox per dataset.

I'll attach two sample user IDs in a follow-up. Also looping Carlos (IT security) who wants to see a proposed SLA and the exact log fields you can provide.

Katie
Director, Product Security
Nova Health

Soojin / Marissa — thanks for the ping. High-level legal position: we can add a pilot-scoped contractual addendum that specifies a per-tenant backup retention override to 30 days and an operational purge commitment, provided both of the following are true:

1) Nova defines the exact tenant IDs/datasets in writing (so the scope is auditable).
2) Nova accepts a consented carve-out that for the duration of the pilot Redwood may retain metadata required for debugging for up to 90 days (we can minimize fields to non-PII).

I want the contract language to be explicit about what "purge" means (hot cache + persistent object store + remove references in index/metadata) and a statement that cold immutable archive deletion will be performed where feasible, with an evidence artifact explaining feasibility limits.

Marissa — can you draft the operational text we can use in the addendum? Include timelines (72-hour purge job post-request, 30-day auto-rollover) and the exact log fields: request_id, requestor_email, tenant_id, deletion_timestamp, job_run_id, affected_paths. If cold archive deletion cannot be guaranteed in some storage backends, we should provide a documented exception path (evidence + manual attestation).

I'll get legal to draft the clause and circle back with a redline.

—Rishi
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

All — attaching a short operational summary and a sample evidence payload we can provide (I included it in RTBF_Process_Summary_v2.pdf but copying the key parts here):

Operational summary (pilot path):
- Tenant scoping: Nova provides tenant_ids for pilot in writing.
- Deletion workflow: 
  1) Customer-initiated RTBF request created -> queued (0–15 min).
  2) Delete job runs against hot stores & model caches (within 72h).
  3) Snapshot purge job scheduled on next retention window; for pilot tenants we will force purge within 30 days.
  4) Cold-archive: we will attempt to remove objects; if backend constraints prevent deletion, we provide a manual attestation plus export of the object manifest and deletion request IDs.

Evidence payload (fields we will provide):
- request_id
- tenant_id
- user_id
- deletion_timestamp
- actor_id (service account)
- affected_tables/paths
- job_run_id + exit status
- hash of deletion artifact (for integrity)

Caveats: For certain third-party backup destinations we may only be able to provide evidence of a deletion request and the provider's acknowledgement (some storage providers implement immutable backups with retention controls we do not override automatically). We'll flag any such items in the evidence bundle.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Katie/Carlos: send two sample tenant_ids and two sample user_ids in the template.
2) Soojin: schedule a 30-minute technical call with Nova engineers to walk through the purge runbook and log schema (I can join).
3) Rishi: once we have the tenant list, legal will draft the pilot addendum and circulate a redline.

I'll also upload the evidence template to the shared drive and link it in the HubSpot deal.

Marissa
Head of Privacy Ops, Redwood Inference
